BiblicalUsage: Abihu is the second son of Aaron, named with his brothers Nadab, Eleazar, and Ithamar. He goes up the mountain with Moses and sees God; and then, with Nadab, he offers ‘strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not’, and fire from the LORD devours them both.
TheologicalSignificance: Abihu stood on the mountain and saw God — and still died for offering strange fire. I believe his story is the sharpest warning in the priesthood: nearness to God is not a licence, and worship is only accepted on His terms, not mine.
